rows.name: APITRX
rows.model_source: Their order endpoint takes no price at all - only apikey, address, energy value and hours - and a separate endpoint publishes the rate per term: web.apitrx.com/price
rows.terms_source: API docs enumerate the rental period as 1/24/72/168/336/720 hours (1h, 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, 30d) and the published price table runs 1 Hour / 24 Hour / 72 Hour / 7 Day / 14 Day / 30 Day — no sub-hour period and no 240-hour one: apitrx.com/en/pages/energy.html
rows.auth_seen_26_11: apikey from their Telegram bot, sent as a query parameter

rows.name: CatFee
rows.model_source: A flat published rate - "Each 3 TRX = 65,000 energy" - and their order method carries quantity, duration and receiver but no price field: docs.catfee.io/en/getting-started/quickstart
rows.auth_seen_26_11: API key from the CatFee website account; docs also list webhooks and idempotency

rows.name: EnergyFather
rows.model_source: Their own FAQ: "Rental price at EnergyFather does not change depending on the time of day or anything else", and the buy endpoint returns the cost rather than accepting one: energyfather.com/faq/buying-energy-faq
rows.terms_source: docs: "Currently, only 6 periods are valid: 1 hour and 1, 3, 7, 15, 30 days."

rows.name: iTRX
rows.model_source: A keyless endpoint publishes the whole tier table - tiered_pricing with a price per period - and the order form has no price field: itrx.io/api/v1/frontend/index-data
rows.terms_source: The Quick Rent form offers exactly four durations — 1H, 1D, 3D, 30D — so it steps straight from three days to thirty: itrx.io/en

rows.name: MeFree
rows.model_source: One announced rate per transfer in their own order form: <option value="3">3 TRX / 1 hour</option> at mefree.net
rows.terms_source: Their order API documents period as 0 = fast charge, 1 = one hour, 2 = 1 day, 3 = 3 days, and 4 to 30 = that many days: docs.mefree.net/api/create-order

rows.name: NETTS
rows.model_source: They quote one rate to everyone through their own price feed and the buyer names nothing: netts.io/api/get-current-prices.php
rows.terms_source: The duration selector on their own order form lists 1 hour and every whole day from 1 to 30, ten days included (<option value="864000">10 days</option>): netts.io

rows.name: re:Fee
rows.model_source: Their published API calculates the cost for you - /precountOrder takes token, days and volume and returns the price: api.refee.bot/docs

rows.name: RentTron
rows.model_source: A keyless endpoint publishes the rate and the order method takes only addresses and amounts: renttron.com/api/prices
rows.terms_source: RentTron sells one product and states its length itself: 'Receive energy instantly upon TRX payment confirmation for 1 hour': renttron.com/en

rows.name: TR Energy
rows.model_source: Their API publishes period_prices_energy and the order body carries no price field at all, only amount and period: tr.energy
rows.terms_source: Their order form offers 15 minutes, 60 minutes, 24 hours and 72 hours (plus a renewing 72 hours); nothing longer: tr.energy/en

rows.name: TronZap
rows.model_source: Their services endpoint publishes prices and the order call takes address, amount and duration with no price field: docs.tronzap.com/api/services.html
rows.terms_source: docs: "Currently only 1 hour is supported for energy, bandwidth, and resource_bundle."
rows.auth_seen_26_11: API token + API secret; signature = sha256(request body + secret)

rows.name: Tronex Energy
rows.model_source: Their documented method prices the order for you: POST /api/v1/precountOrder takes days and volume and returns price and total: tronex.gitbook.io/docs/api-documentation/api-v1/energy
rows.terms_source: Their pricing API accepts 1h, 1d, 3d and 7d and rejects everything else, so there is no ten-day rental to price: api.tronex.energy
rows.auth_seen_26_11: X-API-KEY header on every request; HMAC signing optional per account

rows.name: TronEnergize
rows.model_source: Every order in their public book carries the seller's stake and the APY he earns for filling it, and their price feed is named minprices — a floor the buyer has to clear, not a posted rate: tronenergize.com/api/v1/market
rows.terms_source: their price feed, keys in 3-second blocks

rows.name: Tronify
rows.model_source: Their order method carries an orderPrice the buyer sets, inside a floor and ceiling the platform publishes, and a seller closes that specific order. A fixed-price instant mode runs beside it: docs-tron.en.tronify.io/tron-api/create-trx-energy-order
rows.terms_source: Their order API takes pledgeMinute 10, pledgeHour 1 or 3, and pledgeDay 1 to 30 — ten days is a valid day count, fifteen minutes is not a valid minute one: docs-tron.en.tronify.io

rows.name: TronMax
rows.model_source: The buyer types a price and their own form rejects anything under the per-duration minimum; their public order list shows what actually filled: api.tronmax.io/order/orders

rows.name: TronSave
rows.model_source: Their own documentation calls the price a bid and sorts the market by it: the buy endpoint takes a unitPrice, and SLOW / MEDIUM / FAST are how fast a seller is expected to take it (docs.tronsave.io/concepts/order-types).

rows.name: JustLend DAO — Energy Rental
rows.model_source: Renting here is delegation against refundable deposits, priced by a published formula on a public contract, not by a shop price: docs.justlend.org/developers/energy_rental
rows.terms: by the hour or by the day, up to 30 days
rows.terms_source: JustLend DAO's own docs: energy is rented 'by the hour or by the day, with a maximum single rental period of 30 days': docs.justlend.org
rows.auth_seen_26_11: no platform key: a contract call from your own wallet (their example uses TronWeb)

rows.name: Ergon
rows.model_source: Rentals run through a contract with a refundable deposit worth one day's rent, and the rate comes from a public method rather than from the buyer: ergon.ustx.io/php/ergonGetPrice.php
rows.terms_source: Ergon quotes a tiered TRX per 1M energy PER DAY rate; the published price is rate x days x energy / 1e6. Rentals run 1-7d, so 15m/1h and 10d are not offered. The refundable 1-day security deposit is not included. Their order form takes any amount you type in, above a 100,000 floor; the 100,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 / 2,000,000 buttons beside it only fill the field. So both of the board's volumes are the same per-million rate, pro rata, and only the 65k one is under their minimum.
